cwe_name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code directly uses attacker-controlled CONTENT_LENGTH to allocate memory for reading request body without size limits, then processes it through ASN.1 decoder which may allocate additional resources

connection.evidence: Direct path: env["CONTENT_LENGTH"] (attacker-controlled) → int() conversion → env["wsgi.input"].read(length) → codec.decode()

diff_causality.evidence: This line introduces the vulnerable pattern by reading from wsgi.input using unvalidated length. Reverting would prevent the uncontrolled resource allocation at this specific point.

security_control.evidence: Required control: Request size limiting/throttling. Required because CWE-770 specifically addresses unlimited resource allocation. Existing controls checked: None observed for CONTENT_LENGTH validation. Deficiency evidence: No bounds checking on CONTENT_LENGTH value before using it for memory allocation.
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-770 requires limiting resource allocation to prevent exhaustion attacks; using unvalidated attacker-controlled length for memory allocation violates this principle
existing_controls_checked: No observed CONTENT_LENGTH validation or size limits
security_control.deficiency_evidence: CONTENT_LENGTH is converted to integer without any bounds checking, allowing arbitrarily large values to be used for memory allocation

concrete_impact.evidence: Memory exhaustion leading to denial of service through allocation of large request buffers and ASN.1 decoding overhead

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the application would not read and decode request bodies using attacker-controlled CONTENT_LENGTH, preventing the uncontrolled resource allocation vulnerability at this specific point.
supporting_evidence: CONTENT_LENGTH HTTP header is attacker-controlled and converted to integer without validation
env["wsgi.input"].read(length) allocates memory based on unvalidated length parameter
ASN.1 decoder (codec.decode) processes the potentially large input, consuming additional resources
unresolved_facts: Maximum request size limit imposed by WSGI server configuration
Behavior of env["wsgi.input"].read() with negative or zero length values
Internal resource limits within the ASN.1 decoder implementation
review_comment: The code uses attacker-controlled CONTENT_LENGTH without validation to allocate memory for request processing, enabling memory exhaustion attacks. Add server-side request size limits by validating CONTENT_LENGTH against a reasonable maximum (e.g., 1MB) before reading from the input stream.
